title: The Impact of Using a ChatGPT-based Application to Enhance Saudi Students’ EFL Vocabulary Learning
venue: International Journal of Language and Literary Studies
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a ChatGPT-based application can improve English as a Foreign Language (EFL) vocabulary learning among Saudi secondary students, and whether students hold positive attitudes toward using such a tool. The study is motivated by the limited empirical evidence on generative AI for language learning, especially vocabulary acquisition, and by the potential of ChatGPT to provide interactive, personalized, and immediate feedback beyond what is typically feasible in traditional classrooms.

The intervention was a custom-built application called “Learn With AI,” developed using Flutter and powered by ChatGPT. It included preloaded target vocabulary from the students’ textbook and several structured modes: Meaning, Sentences, Story, and Practice; the procedures section also mentions a Chat mode. These modes used embedded prompts to generate Arabic translations, simple English explanations, example sentences, short stories, and multiple-choice practice with feedback. The control group studied the same vocabulary using traditional pen-and-paper materials containing the same vocabulary list, Arabic translations, and simple English definitions, but without interactivity. Both groups also received periodic Telegram reminders from the researcher during the experimental period.

The participants were female second-year public high school students in Qassim, Saudi Arabia, aged 16–17. The study used a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with an experimental group (27 students) and a control group (30 students), for a total of 57 participants. The intervention lasted eight weeks. Vocabulary learning was measured with a 54-item multiple-choice pretest/posttest, and student attitudes were measured with an Arabic questionnaire administered after the intervention.

The paper concludes that the ChatGPT-based application significantly improved vocabulary outcomes relative to the traditional comparison condition. The groups did not differ significantly at pretest (t = -1.638, p = 0.111), but the experimental group outperformed the control group at posttest (t = -3.076, p = 0.0036) and showed significantly larger gains (t = -2.262, p = 0.0278). Students also reported positive attitudes toward the application, describing it as motivating, comfortable, and helpful for vocabulary learning. The authors argue that ChatGPT’s interactivity, varied contextualization of words, and immediate personalized feedback make it a promising tool for EFL vocabulary instruction, while noting the need for larger and more diverse future studies.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental pretest-posttest comparison with a control group and statistical testing, which is stronger than correlational work. However, it has notable credibility concerns: small sample, non-randomized groups, female-only sample, limited reporting of implementation/dosage detail, and no standardized effect sizes or variance estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings indicate a statistically significant positive effect on EFL vocabulary learning and positive attitudes in a priority population (secondary EFL learners), but impact magnitude is unclear because no standardized effect size or confidence intervals are reported. The sample is also small and context-specific, limiting certainty about practical impact size.

interventions.use_case: A ChatGPT-based EFL vocabulary-learning application ('Learn With AI') for Saudi public high school students, offering word meaning, sentence, story, practice, and free-chat modes with immediate interactive feedback around 54 target textbook vocabulary items.

The same app also functions as software-delivered vocabulary instruction through preloaded word lists, multiple presentation modes, and practice activities, compared against paper-based traditional vocabulary study materials.

finding.finding_summary: In this quasi-experimental comparison, the ChatGPT-based vocabulary app outperformed the traditional paper-based condition on a 54-item vocabulary multiple-choice post-test among Saudi high school EFL learners. The experimental group (n=27) showed mean improvement of 12.2 points versus 7.4 points in the control group (n=30); reported t-tests showed no pretest difference (t=-1.638, p=0.111) but significant post-test differences (t=-3.076, p=0.0036) and significant difference-score advantages for the experimental group (t=-2.262, p=0.0278).
finding.measure: Researcher-developed 54-item multiple-choice vocabulary pre-test/post-test based on textbook target words

finding.finding_summary: Students reported broadly positive attitudes toward using the ChatGPT-based app for vocabulary learning, with large majorities selecting strongly agree/agree across motivation, enjoyment, comfort, and perceived usefulness items. For example, 86.95% agreed/strongly agreed they enriched vocabulary knowledge, 73.92% felt motivated to use this method after being introduced to ChatGPT, 86.95% enjoyed learning vocabulary with it, and 91.30% found it interesting and motivating for future use.
finding.measure: Follow-up attitude questionnaire (20 Likert-style items reported as percentages) on motivation, enjoyment, comfort, and perceived usefulness
